info.description:
The API of an fvoci server.

## Signing in

`login` answers with a `Set-Cookie` header that carries the session: the cookie `__Host-fvoci_session` where the server is reached over HTTPS, `fvoci_session` over plain HTTP. It is `HttpOnly`, so a page's scripts never see it, and a browser sends it by itself. A client that is no browser may send the cookie's value as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` instead. The operations under `/shared/{containerId}` need no session: they read a shared board with its `readToken`, and look at no session that comes along.

## Requests that change something

Every request whose method is not `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` needs the header `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`, unless it has a bearer token, and is refused with 403 and the reason `csrf` without it. If it has an `Origin` header, the origin must be the server's own (or one the server was configured to accept); otherwise it is refused with 403 and the reason `foreign_origin`.

A page should make these requests with `fetch` in its default mode, `cors`. The server sends its pages with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and under that policy a browser writes `Origin: null` on a changing request of any other mode (`same-origin`, `no-cors`, or a form the browser posts itself), which is refused as a foreign origin.

## Answers

An operation answers 200 with a body, 201 with what it made, or 204 with no body. Every other status comes with a `Problem`, the problem details of RFC 9457, as `application/problem+json`: `type` names the kind of the problem and is the same for every problem of the kind, `title` is its name, `status` repeats the status and `detail` says what went wrong this time. `type` is `/problems/<name>` under the path the server is served at, the address of a page of text about the kind; `/problems` lists them, and so does `x-problem-types` of the schema `Problem`, as they are on a server at the root of its host (a server under a path has that path before each). `reason` tells apart causes a client must tell apart; a problem with a `reason` has the `type` of that name, written with hyphens, and any other the `type` of its status. `errors` lists what of the request was refused, each by a JSON Pointer into the body (`pointer`), the name of a parameter of the query or the path (`parameter`), or the name of a header (`header`). `limit` is the limit that was exceeded: bytes for a body that was too large (413), a count for too many of something. `instance` is the request, `urn:uuid:` and its `requestId`. A session that is missing or over is 401. What the user may not see is 404, as if it were not there; what they may see but not do is 403. A path that is no operation is 404 too, and a method an operation's path does not have is 405.

A request without a session whose JSON body has more than 64 KiB is 413 before it is 401. A body larger than its route reads is 413 with the reason `request_too_large` and the `limit` in bytes.

Any request may be answered 503 with the reason `database_busy`: the database did not take one of its statements in time (another write held the file, or no connection to it was to be had). That statement did nothing and may be taken a moment later. A request of one step may be sent again as it is; of one of several (`completeUpload`, `importArchive`) what was done before stays done, and sent again it is answered as its operation says.

The identifiers of users, workspaces, boards, blocks and categories are UUIDs, written lower-case with hyphens; a client takes every identifier as an opaque string. A `fileId` is no UUID: it is an unguessable name that ends in the file's extension. Times are milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

## Lists

Every list comes in an order, and the description of each operation says which. Where it says nothing else, the order is that of creation, oldest first, and by identifier among what was created in the same millisecond.

## The user's own space

Every account has a space of its own from the moment it is made, however it was made: an organization of the `kind` `personal` with the account as its only member and one workspace, which `getMyWorkspaces` lists with that `kind`. Its workspace is a workspace like another to the operations under `/w/{workspaceId}`: boards, wikis, files, search, the trash, export and import, and sharing by a public link (`setSharing`) work in it as anywhere. It has no name (a client calls it by the reader's language) and takes none.

What it has not is other people, and anybody to administer it. Its identifier is 404 for every operation under `/org/{orgId}` (the organization and its settings, its members, its workspaces, joining one as an administrator, its audit log, its provider of sign-ins), for its owner as for anybody else, and no answer of those operations names it. Under its workspace these are 404, as for a workspace that is not there: `createInvitation`, `getInvitations`, `revokeInvitation`, `emailInvitation`, `setGuestInvitations`, `setWorkspaceRole`, `removeWorkspaceMember`, the operations on teams (`/w/{workspaceId}/teams` and what is under it) and on the teams of a board or a wiki (`/w/{workspaceId}/containers/{containerId}/teams`). It has no login page (`getLoginOptions`) and no sign-in through a provider starts for it. Nothing in it is moved to or from another organization but by export and import, and no reference reaches into it from outside or out of it. What changes in it is told to nobody else: the server's operator is posted no block of it (`block_change_webhooks`), and it is in no audit log anybody but its owner reads.

An account that was made by a sign-in through an organization's provider has no password (`hasPassword` of `getMe`), and until it has one its space is reached by any session of the account. It is given one by `setPassword`, so that its person reaches the space when they are no longer in that organization. Once the account has a password, the space takes only sessions that have shown it: one made with it (`login`), and one made through a provider that gave it since (`confirmPassword`). A provider is an organization's, and whoever holds it could make a session of the account. To a session made through a provider that has not given the password, the routes under the space's `/w/{workspaceId}` then answer 401 with the reason `password_sign_in_required`, `getMyWorkspaces` lists the space with `passwordRequired` true, `getMyMemberships` leaves its boards out, `getAccountDeletion` names it without what is in it, and the websocket follows nothing of it for such a session (`contracts/websocket.md`). The session stays and opens what it opened of the organizations.

There are two ways in from there. `confirmPassword` keeps the session: it gives the password once, and from then until it ends the session opens the space beside what it opened before, so that somebody whose organization takes only sessions made through its provider (`sso_required`) goes between that organization and the space without signing in again. Signing in with the password (`login`) opens the space too, in a new session, which such an organization then asks to sign in through its provider again. What a session confirmed opens the account's own space and nothing else: not what is another account's, and nothing of an organization that takes only sessions made through a provider other than the session's own. It goes with the session: a change of the password (`changePassword`, a reset, the operator's) ends the account's other sessions, as it always did, and what they confirmed with them. What is shared from the space by a public link is read without a session, and is not closed so.

It goes with its account: `getAccountDeletion` names it among `organizations` always, and while the account waits to be deleted it is closed with the account: what is shared from it by a public link answers 404 as a link that is not there, and answers again if the deletion is cancelled.

## Bodies edited together

While people edit a card's body together the server holds it as a Y document. What it refuses of an editor has the reason `update_refused`, `update_out_of_step`, `update_too_large` or `document_too_large`; `too_many_documents` and `document_unavailable` say that it cannot take the document for now. A write of a card's whole body here (a patch of the card or of blocks, a card stored again) first writes to the card what its editors typed: a `readAt` from before that is refused with 409, and if it cannot be written the write is refused with `document_unavailable`. The editors themselves speak to the server over the websocket, whose messages name the same reasons (`contracts/websocket.md`); `document_read_only`, `connection_too_slow`, `too_many_documents_joined`, `document_full`, `too_many_connections_joined` and `too_many_frames` come only there. The page of each kind says when it comes. `search_not_configured` comes from none of these operations: only from the reindex of the administration socket, on a server configured without a search server (a search there searches its database).

## Request bodies

A request schema lists the members a request is for. A member that is not required may be left out. `null` is a value only of a member whose schema allows it, and is then none; `null` for any other member is refused with 400, as a value of another type is. A member the schema marks as required is one the request cannot do without; where the server takes a missing one as empty instead of refusing the request, the result is that of the empty value (a login without a password is a failed login). A body with members the schema does not list is mostly not refused for them. The exceptions: `patchUserSettings` and `patchMe` refuse every member they do not know, `createBoard` and `createCategory` refuse an `id`, and `setSharing` refuses a `token`.
info.title: fvoci

get.description:
Where a provider sends the browser back to: each organization has an address of its
own, its provider's `redirectUri`, and a sign-in started for one organization does
not finish at another's address, nor with an `iss` (RFC 9207) other than the
provider's, before any code is exchanged. The sign-in is taken by its `state`, once, and only from the
browser that started it; another browser takes nothing. The code is
exchanged for an ID token, whose signature, issuer, audience, time and nonce are
checked. The person is known by the issuer and the subject: an account of theirs
signs in, and somebody who has none gets one, if the organization lets newcomers in
and no account has their email address. A registration that waits for that address
to be confirmed (`register`, `acceptInvitation`) stands in nobody's way. Where the
provider vouches for the address, one made by a link of this organization is
removed with the sign-in, new account or known: the use it took of the link is
given back, and the link mailed for it confirms nothing any more. A registration
of its own, or by a link of another organization, stays, and so does any at a
trial of pending settings and at a sign-in that carries over. The session comes in the `Set-Cookie`
header, and the browser goes to the web app (303). A sign-in that was started to
link sets no session: the browser goes to the web app with `oidc_linked=1` in the
query. A trial of the provider's pending settings (`startOidcTrial`) that ends well
makes them the provider's and sets the session, made through them, and the browser
goes to the organization's page (`/org/{orgId}`) with `oidc_pending=applied`; one
that fails changes nothing, and goes there with `oidc_pending_error` naming the
reason as `oidc_error` does (among them `oidc_trial_account` and
`oidc_trial_stale`).

Otherwise the browser goes to the login page of the organization (`/login?org=…`),
with the reason of what went wrong in `oidc_error`, by the name of its problem
(`oidc_state_invalid` as `oidc-state-invalid`): `oidc_state_invalid`, `oidc_denied`,
`oidc_token_refused`, `oidc_token_invalid`, `oidc_email_missing`,
`oidc_email_unverified`, `oidc_email_taken`, `oidc_join_closed`,
`oidc_identity_taken`, `oidc_email_mismatch`, `oidc_carry_over_refused` or
`oidc_unavailable`.

While the organization keeps the provider it moved away from (`former` of its
provider), a sign-in that vouches for somebody who has no account makes none: what
the provider said is held for this browser for ten minutes, under a cookie of its
own, and the browser goes to the login page with `oidc_held=1`, which asks whether
the person had an account: `startOidcCarryOver` if they had, `finishHeldOidcLogin`
if not. A sign-in through the former provider, which `startOidcCarryOver` starts,
comes back here too: it sets a session only by carrying the held sign-in over.
Where nothing is carried over it goes to the login page with
`oidc_carry_over_refused`, and where the sign-in itself failed (refused by the
former provider, its token not taken, not this browser's) with that reason, as
any sign-in does. An account that comes into the organization by the sign-in, as a
member, is given its welcome board unless it has one (`onboard` says more): in the
language of its settings, or else in the one `Accept-Language` prefers.

post.description:
For the login page, after a sign-in through the provider of the organization `org`
was held for this browser (`finishOidcLogin` sent it to the login page with
`oidc_held=1`): for somebody who had an account before the organization moved to
this provider. Starts a sign-in through the organization's former provider and
answers where the page sends the browser, with the cookie of that sign-in. When
the browser comes back (`finishOidcLogin`), the former provider must vouch for an
identity tied to an account in use that has a place in the organization (a member,
or a guest of one of its workspaces in use, who joins nothing by it): the held
identity is then tied to that account, which is recorded in the organization's
audit log (`oidc_identity_carried_over`), and a session made through the
organization's provider is set. Both identities are shown by signing in, so no
email address is compared. The former provider signs nobody in otherwise: no
session is made through it.

409 with the reason `oidc_carry_over_refused` if no sign-in of the organization is
held for this browser (none, ended after ten minutes, taken already, or held for
another browser), the organization keeps no former provider any more, or `org`
names no organization that is signed in to; the same
reason comes back on the login page (`oidc_error`) when the return carried nothing
over. 409 with `oidc_unavailable` if the former provider cannot be reached; 429
when this address made too many sign-ins of late.

post.description:
For the login page of the server, as a request of its own, not an address a browser
is sent to: like every request that changes something it needs the header
`X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` and no foreign `Origin`, which a page of another
site cannot send, so that no such page can sign a browser in to an account of its
choosing. Starts a sign-in for the organization `org` and answers where the page
sends the browser (the provider), with a cookie that ties the sign-in to this
browser, and ten minutes to come back. 409 with the reason `oidc_unavailable` if
the organization has no provider that is on, or it cannot be reached; 429 when
this address made too many sign-ins of late.

With `linkPassword` in the body the sign-in links: it needs the session of the
browser's cookie (401 without; a bearer token does not do, as the browser comes back
with its cookie), whose account's password that is, and when the browser comes back, who the provider
vouches for is tied to that account in place of signing in (`getMyIdentities`);
after that the provider signs in to the account. No account is made and none is
joined to another: an identity that is another account's is refused
(`oidc_identity_taken`), and so is one whose email address, as the provider has
checked it, is not the account's own (`oidc_email_mismatch`): the password ties no
other person of the provider to the account. It ends only in the browser that started it and still has
the session it was started from (`oidc_state_invalid` otherwise). A wrong password
is 400 with the reason `invalid_credentials`, naming `/linkPassword`, counted as a
wrong one of `changePassword` is; an account without a password is 409 with the
reason `password_not_set`. The session need not open the organization. A body with
another member, or a `linkPassword` that is no text, is 400 naming it: what was
meant to link does not sign in instead.

post.description:
Consumes the token of the link mailed by `requestEmailChange`, within a day of
the mail and seven days of the request: the address the link was mailed to becomes
the account's. No session is needed and none is made: the link shows that its
holder reads the new address, and the password was given when the change was
asked for. From then on reset links go to the new address and `login` finds the
account by it; the reset links mailed to the address before end, and that address
is mailed a notice that it is the account's no more, which names the account and
nothing of the new address, with a link that gives the account that address back
(`revertEmailChange`). The account's sessions go on.

A link is used once. A token that is missing, used, ended, replaced by a newer
mail or request, or taken back (`cancelEmailChange`), one of an account that is no
longer in use or whose password was set anew since, and one whose address somebody
else took meanwhile are all answered 400 naming `token` in `errors`, and change
nothing: which of them it was is not said. Requests are counted by where they come
from, as registrations are, and too many are 429. While the server's queue of
recovery mail has no place for the notice, the change is not made and the answer
is 503: the link stays as it was.

429.description: Too many requests from where this one comes from.

Retry-After.description: How many seconds to wait before trying again.

503.description: The notice to the address before has no place yet: nothing was changed.

default.description: The request was refused, or failed. post.summary: Confirm the new email address of an account

post.description:
Consumes the token of the link mailed, with the notice of `confirmEmailChange`, to
the address the account had until then (`<server_url>/revert-email#<token>`, for
seven days from the change, used once): for the owner of an account whose address
was moved by somebody who knew the password. No session is needed and none is made.
Opening the page of the link changes nothing; this request does, all of it at once:

- the address the link was mailed to is the account's again and is answered as
  `email`, unless another account or a registration has it by now: then the
  account's email address is cleared (so the address set after this change can no
  longer recover the account, and an operator helps recover it), and `email` is
  left out;
- every session of the account ends, and its live connections close;
- the account's password is locked: `login`, and every request that asks for the
  password, refuses it as a wrong one, until a new one is set through a reset link
  (`requestPasswordReset`, mailed to the restored address) or by the operator;
- any single sign-on identity linked to the account after this link was created is
  removed; identities already linked at or before that time stay and sign in as
  they did, opening no more;
- the change of address that waited ends, and so do the account's reset links and
  the links of this kind mailed after this one. Those mailed before it stand.

The address the account had until then is mailed a notice that names nothing of
the address it has now. No reset link is mailed by this request.

While a link stands, the address it was mailed to is held for the account: another
account's change of address, `register` and `acceptInvitation` are answered as for
an address an account has. Nothing ends a link but its use, its seven days and the
erasing of the account: not a newer change of address, nor taking a change back,
nor a password changed, set or reset, nor asking to delete the account.

A token that is missing, used, ended, of a link mailed after one that was used, or
of an account that is being erased, is 400 naming `token` in `errors`, and changes
nothing: which of them it was is not said. Requests are counted by where they come
from, as registrations are, and too many are 429.

post.summary: Give an account the email address it had back

post.description:
Consumes the token of the link mailed to a registration's address, within a day of
the mail and seven days of the registration: makes the account, and the
organization and first workspace it registered with if it named one, and signs it in. The session
comes in the `Set-Cookie` header, as from `login`, and the answer says where the
account was let in. A link is used once, and a newer mail of the same registration
ends the links before it. A missing, ended, used or replaced token answers 400,
naming `token` in `errors`.

Only who registered finishes a registration, so that nobody is signed in to an
account whose password somebody else chose. In the browser the registration was
made from, which the cookie of `register` or `acceptInvitation` shows, the token is
enough. Anywhere else a token that would confirm is answered 403 with the reason
`password_required`, and the request is sent again with `password`, the password the
registration was made with: a wrong one is the 401 of `login` (`invalid_credentials`),
counted with the failed logins to the registration's user name, and too many are
429. A request that is refused so leaves the link as it was. Nothing is asked of a
token that confirms nothing, so the answers tell no more of whether a registration
waits than the token does.

On a server that takes one organization and has its first user by now,
the registration is removed and the answer is 403 with the reason
`invitation_required`. A registration made by the link of an invitation
(`acceptInvitation`) is let in as the acceptance would have let it in, and the answer
names the board of a guest's link (`containerId`); if the link lets nobody in any more
(revoked, or who made it may no longer invite), the registration is removed and the
answer is 404 with the reason `invitation_unavailable`. Requests are counted by where they come from, as
registrations are, and too many are 429.

An account that a link for members lets in so is given its welcome board in the
workspace, unless it has one (`onboard` says more): written in the `language` of
the acceptance if that was English or Korean, or else in English.

200.description: The account was made and signed in, and was let in here.

429.description: Too many requests from where this one comes from, or too many wrong passwords at the registration's user name.

Retry-After.description: How many seconds to wait before trying again.

post.description:
Answers 204 with an empty body whether or not a registration that is not confirmed
yet has the user name (or else the address), and whatever became of the message;
lookup and delivery run in the background. A new link ends the one before it. A
registration's address is sent at most `mail_reset_per_account_hour` messages an
hour, its first link counted: more requests are answered the same, send nothing
and lock nothing. Requests are limited by where they come from, with the requests
for a reset link (429). A request that names neither is 400. A server that sends no
mail answers 404; one that sends mail answers also after `emailVerification` was
turned off, for the registrations made while it was on.

Answers the text `Hello`, and asks nothing of what the server depends on: the check

post.description:
Lets somebody into the workspace the link of `token` leads into, and answers where
that is. A request with a session lets in the user of the session, and names no
`account` (400 if it does). A request without one makes the `account` it names and
lets that in: the account's members are checked as `register` checks them (400,
with `errors`, which name them under `/account`), and a name or an email address
that is taken is 409 with the reason `username_taken` or `email_taken`. Accepting
does not sign in.

A member's link makes the account a member of the workspace and of its
organization; who is a guest of the workspace becomes a member, and who works there
already stays what they are. A guest's link puts the account on its board, in the
link's role or the higher one the account has there: who is no member of the
workspace becomes a guest of it (and no member of its organization), and who is one
stays what they are in it. The answer names the board then (`containerId`). The account
is made, the membership stored and the use of the link counted together or not at
all, and an acceptance that changes nothing uses nothing of the link.

On a server that asks for the email address of a registration to be confirmed
(`emailVerification` of `getLoginOptions`), a new `account` waits for its address,
unless the link was made for one recipient of a mailed guest link at that address,
which the mail proves: the answer is 202 with no body, nobody is let in, and the
link mailed to the address (`completeEmailVerification`) makes the account and lets
it in, as this acceptance would have, and signs it in. The 202 sets the cookie of
the browser the registration was made from, as `register` does. The registration counts as a
use of the link from the start, so a link for one guest lets nobody else in
meanwhile, and it holds its name and address as an account would. Not confirmed in
seven days, it is removed and gives the use back. A new `account` from the browser
of a registration that waits still (by this link, another, or `register`) replaces
that registration: its name and address are free for the account, and the use it
took of a link is given back, so that a link for one guest takes the same person
again with the address put right. `language` is the language of the
mail (English or Korean).

A session that the link's organization does not take (it takes no password,
`ssoRequired`, and the session was not made through its provider) is 401 with the
reason `sso_required` and its `orgId`, and lets nobody in.

A token that lets nobody in is 404 with the reason `invitation_unavailable`,
whatever is wrong with it: there is no such link, it ended, it was used as often as
it may be, it was revoked, or who made it may no longer invite. Requests are counted
by where they come from, and too many are 429.

An account that a link for members lets in is given its welcome board in the
workspace, a private board of its own, unless it has one (`onboard` says more):
written in the language of the account's settings, or else in `language` for an
account made here, if that is English or Korean, or else in the one
`Accept-Language` prefers. An account whose address is confirmed first is given
it then (`completeEmailVerification`).

One page of what the user of the session was told, in every organization the
session opens, the newest first (by `updateAt`): that somebody mentioned them in a
card, a page, a unit or a comment (`mention`), gave them a card (`assignment`), or
commented on a card, a page or a unit they watch (`comment`; one named in that comment

user's own space, nor of a kind they switched off (`notifyMentions`,
`notifyAssignments`, `notifyComments` of `patchUserSettings`): what is off is not made
at all.

Whoever writes a card, a page or a unit, is given a card, or comments on one watches
it (`createSubscription`), until they end that (`deleteSubscription`). What happens to
one card, page or unit, of one kind, within an hour of the first of it, is one
notification: `times` and `people` count it, `actorId` and `commentId` say the
latest, and it is unread again. One person makes a hundred new ones for another
within an hour at most; past that, what they do joins only those there.

A notification is made only for somebody who reads the card, page or unit at that
time, and each one listed is asked again: its `subject` says what it is about, as
that is now, only where the user reads it now with this session. Where they do not
(it is in the trash or gone, or they left the container or the workspace) `subject` is
`null`, and nothing says what it was about, where or by whom. Such a one is still
listed, and counted while unread.

What an organization that takes only sessions made through its provider told the
user is left out for a session made otherwise, as `getMyMemberships` leaves its
boards out: it is not listed, not counted, and not marked as read by such a
session, and it is there again for a session made through the provider.

A notification that was read is kept for ninety days, and a user has ten thousand
at most: past that the oldest go, those that were read first.

put.description:
Sets the organization's `OpenID Connect` provider, in place of the one it has. The
discovery document of an issuer that is not the organization's already is read
first: it must name the issuer exactly and have
`https` endpoints, or the request is 400 with the reason `oidc_issuer_unverified`
and `errors` naming `/issuer`. The server reaches only `https` addresses, follows no
redirect, and reaches only public addresses unless its configuration lets it
(`oidc_allow_private_addresses`).

`clientSecret` left out keeps the stored secret while the issuer and the client stay
the same; with another issuer or client it is required when a secret is stored (400,
`required` at `/clientSecret`), as the secret is the old client's. The empty string
stores none. The secret is stored sealed with the server's key and never answered:
without the key the request is 409 with the reason `secret_key_required`. `autoJoin`
and `enabled` left out stay as they are, also for another issuer or client, and are
on when the organization has no provider.

While the organization takes no password and the request keeps it so, another
issuer, client or secret is not taken at once: it is saved aside as the provider's
`pending` settings (in place of pending ones there are), and people go on signing
in through the provider as it is. A sign-in through the pending settings
(`startOidcTrial`) that ends well makes them the provider's; `deleteOidcPending`
throws them away. The secret of the pending settings is never answered either. What
else the request changes (`autoJoin`) is taken at once; `enabled` false is refused
(`sso_enforced`). While the organization takes a password a change is taken at
once, and a change of what signing in takes throws pending settings away.

`ssoRequired` true makes the organization take no password: from the next request
on, what is the organization's (the routes under `/w/{workspaceId}` and
`/org/{orgId}`, and `setUserAdmin` where the organization is the instance's own, the
oldest) answers 401 with the reason `sso_required` to every session that was not
made through this provider, `getMyMemberships` leaves its boards out for one, and
the websocket follows none of its workspaces for one. The sessions stay, and open
what is of other organizations. It is switched on by a
session that was itself made through this provider, switched on, as it is stored
(`canRequireSso`), by a request that does not change its issuer, client, secret or
`enabled`, or the request is 409 with the reason `sso_unproven`: who asks has then
shown that it lets them in. A `clientSecret` sent as it is stored is no change.
While it is on, the provider is not switched off (`enabled` false) and not removed:
409 with the reason `sso_enforced`, unless the same request switches `ssoRequired`
off. Left out it stays as it is,
and is off when the organization has no provider. A provider changed by another request
since this one read it is 409, to be read and sent again. The answer's `redirectUri`
is the address to register with the provider, exactly: the organization's own,
`…/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback/{orgId}`, the same before the provider is set and after
it is changed.

post.description:
Starts a sign-in through the pending settings (`pending` of the provider), as
`startOidcLogin` starts one through the provider: it answers where the page sends
the browser, with the cookie of the sign-in. When the browser comes back
(`finishOidcLogin`) and the sign-in ends well, in the account of the administrator
who started it, the pending settings become the provider's, at a new revision that the
new session proves (`canRequireSso`); another issuer ends the sessions of the one
before, and keeps the provider before as the `former` one. A sign-in that fails
changes nothing, and no trial makes an account.

Whose account it ends in: the identity the pending settings vouch for must be tied
to the account of the administrator who started the trial. One that is another
account's, or that administrator administering the organization no more, is
refused with `oidc_trial_account`. One that is tied to no account, as an
administrator's is at an issuer the organization moves to, is tied to their own
account by the trial, in the transaction that applies the settings and recorded
(`oidc_identity_bound`), only if the trial was started from a session made through
the organization's provider as it is stored, the browser comes back with that
session, and it comes back no more than five minutes after that session was made
(`bindsIdentityUntil` of the pending settings): who only holds a session cannot
sign in through the provider again, and ties nothing. Otherwise it is refused with
`oidc_trial_stale`: sign in through the provider again (`startOidcLogin`) and
finish the trial within five minutes. Pending
settings of the same issuer tie nothing.

409 with the reason `oidc_unavailable` if there are no pending settings, the
provider is off, or their issuer cannot be reached; 429 when this address made too
many sign-ins of late.

post.description:
Consumes a reset token before its one-hour expiry and sets the new password.
All of the account's sessions and WebSocket connections end, and so do its other
reset links, as they do when the password is changed or set by an operator. The sign-in
lock of the account, at its user name and its email, ends, and so does the wait of the
address that finished the reset. An account that waits to be deleted waits still:
signing in with the new password shows the way back (`getAccountDeletion`), and
taking the deletion back is the person's own act there. A missing, expired or already
used token answers the same 400, naming `token` in `errors`, and so does the token of
an account whose erasing began.

post.description:
Answers 204 with an empty body for an existing account, an absent account and
an account without a password. Lookup and delivery run in the background;
the request never waits for either. Accounts without passwords receive no mail. An
account that waits to be deleted is sent a link as one in use is, so that its person
may sign in and take the deletion back; one whose erasing began, or that was erased,
is sent none (a message already on its way as the erasing begins carries a link that
sets nothing).
Requests are limited by address only, with the login setting of attempts per minute
and a separate counter (429); never by email. An account is sent at most
`mail_reset_per_account_hour` messages an hour: more requests are answered the same
and send nothing. A server that sends no mail answers 404.

get.description:
The check that the server is ready: the database reads the table of the sessions,
which every signed-in request reads, and this process holds the lock of the server
in it; and the file storage takes a small file, gives it back and removes it, each
within two seconds. An answer is kept five seconds; a
request after that waits for the checks made anew, up to two and a half seconds
(a probe's timeout of three seconds is enough), and else gets the answer before.
Neither answer says why a check failed: the log does.

get.summary: Whether the server can serve

post.description:
Makes an account, with its own space (see "The user's own space"), and the
organization it starts if it names one: `organizationName` names the organization
and its first workspace, and the account administers both. Without
`organizationName` (left out, or blank) the account starts with its own space
alone, in no organization, and may start one later (`createOrganization`).

The first user of a server starts the server's own organization and administers
the server too: until there is one (`organizationRequired` of `getLoginOptions`), a
registration without `organizationName` is 400, and `errors` names it with the
reason `required`. On a server that takes one organization (`org_creation` is
`first_user_only`) only the first user registers; everybody after is
refused with 403 and the reason `invitation_required`, whatever else the request
says, and gets in by the link of an invitation (`acceptInvitation`). A name or an
email address that is taken is 409 with the reason `username_taken` or
`email_taken`. Registering does not sign in.

On a server that asks for the email address to be confirmed (`emailVerification` of
`getLoginOptions`), registering makes no account: it answers 202 with no body, and
mails a link to the address, in the language of `language` (English or Korean), that
makes the account, and the organization if it names one, and signs in
(`completeEmailVerification`).
Until then there is nothing of it but its name and address, which are taken as an
account's are, for seven days; a registration that is not confirmed by then is
removed, and its name and address are free again. The 202 sets a cookie that tells
the browser the registration was made from (`fvoci_signup`, `__Host-fvoci_signup`
over HTTPS; `HttpOnly`, for the seven days): no session, it reaches nothing, and
shows `completeEmailVerification` that the browser is the registrant's. A
registration from a browser that has the cookie of one that waits still replaces
that one: whoever mistyped an address registers again at once, under the same user
name, and the link mailed for the first confirms nothing any more. Without the
cookie the name and the address of a registration that waits are taken.

The name and the email address must not be blank, the email address must look like
one, the display name (`displayName`, may be left out) is checked as `patchMe` checks it,
the password must have at least 8 characters and at most 1024 bytes, and the organization
name, where there is one, is read as a display name is; otherwise the
request is 400, and `errors` names every member that is refused, each with
its `reason`: `required`, `invalid_format`, `too_short`, `too_long` or
`invalid_characters`.

202.description: The registration waits for its email address to be confirmed by the link mailed to it.

Set-Cookie.description: The cookie that tells the browser the registration was made from; no session.

429.description: Too many registrations from where this one comes from, or the server has too much password work to do at the moment.

(`firstName`, `lastName`, `latinFirstName`, `latinLastName`), the name they wrote to

server makes it from these (`contracts/name-vectors.json`). A member that is no such
thing, or a value that breaks these rules, is refused (400 naming it) and changes

it, as things are now. The server keeps an administrator (`lastInstanceAdmin`), and

get.summary: What deleting the account comes to

post.description:
Puts the account of the session out of use, to be erased after thirty days
(`graceDays` of `getAccountDeletion`): every session of it ends, this one too, and
its cookie is cleared. Until it is erased, whoever signs in to the account gets a
session that opens nothing (every operation is 401 with the reason
`account_deletion_pending`) but `getAccountDeletion`, `cancelAccountDeletion` and
`logout`. While it waits, the account stays a member of what it is a member of,
shown as one, and what it wrote stays; the links of invitations it made let nobody
in, and it may wait past the thirty days until it is erased.

Erased, the account is gone from every organization, workspace, board and wiki; a
board it alone administered passes to an administrator of its workspace; nothing of
the person is kept, and what it wrote stays under its identifier, which
`getWorkspaceUsersById` answers with no name: the writer is a deleted user. An
organization that has nobody else goes with it, but the server's own first one,
whose only administrator stays as the only one of an organization with other
people does.

`username` is the account's login name, in any letter case: another is 400 naming
`/username`. An account with a password (`proof` is `password`) sends it: a wrong
one is 400 with the reason `invalid_credentials`, naming `/password`, and too many
are 429, as for `changePassword`. An account without one (`proof` is `sign_in`)
asks from a session made through a provider no more than five minutes ago:
otherwise 403 with the reason `sign_in_again`.

An organization that would go with the account and that takes only sessions made
through its provider is asked of such a session: any other is 401 with the reason
`sso_required` and its `orgId`. Leaving an organization is the account's own, and
asked of any session.

The server's only administrator stays (409, reason `last_admin`), and so does the
only administrator of an organization that stays when the account goes: one that
has other people in it, or the server's own first organization (409, reason
`last_org_admin`, `orgId` naming the first such organization): make somebody else
an administrator first.

delete.summary: Take back a change of the email address

post.description:
Asks for the address of the account of the session to become `email`. The
account's `password` is asked for in this request, whatever the session is and
whatever it has shown before: a session alone does not move the address that
password resets are mailed to. An account that has no password (`hasPassword` of
`getMe`) is 409 with the reason `password_not_set`, and sets one first
(`setPassword`). The account of a session that waits to be deleted changes nothing
(401, `account_deletion_pending`).

**On a server that sends mail** (`mailEnabled` of `getClientConfig`) the address
does not change yet. The account waits for the new one to be confirmed: `getMe`
answers it as `pendingEmail`, and a link is mailed to it
(`<server_url>/confirm-email#<token>`, for 24 hours, used once) that
`confirmEmailChange` takes. Until then the account's address is the one it had:
reset links go there, and `login` finds the account by it. An account waits for
one address: a new request replaces the one before, whose link confirms nothing
any more, and so does a change or a reset of the password. What is not confirmed
ends after seven days.

The answer is 204 whether or not another account or a registration has the
address: lookup and mail run once the answer is handed off, nothing is mailed for
an address somebody has, and nothing holds the address until it is confirmed. An
account, and an address, are mailed at most `mail_reset_per_account_hour` such
links an hour; more requests are answered the same and mail nothing.

**On a server that sends no mail** there is nothing to confirm an address with, as
at registration: the address changes with this request, and the answer is 409 with
the reason `email_taken` if another account or a registration has it, in any
letter case. The account's reset links end.

An address is told apart from another as at registration: by its letters in any
case. What is no address, or is the account's already, is 400 naming `email`. A
wrong password is 400 (not 401: the session is good) with the reason
`invalid_credentials`, naming `password`, counted with the failed logins to the
account by its name; too many are 429, also for a login. Requests are also limited
by where they come from, with the requests for a reset link (429). A password that
was changed while this request was under way is 409.

put.description:
Gives the account of the session its first password: for an account that has none
(`hasPassword` of `getMe`), which was made by a sign-in through an organization's
provider. No password is asked for, as there is none: what vouches is a session
made through a provider in the last five minutes. Any other session is 403 with
the reason `sign_in_again`: the account signs in through the provider again
(`startOidcLogin`) and sends the request from the session that comes of it.
From then on the account signs in with it (`login`) by its user name, and reaches
its own space so, also once it is no longer in the organization whose provider made
it; an organization that takes only sessions made through its provider goes on
asking for those (`sso_required`). The account's other sessions end, and this one
goes on under a new cookie, as after `changePassword`.

From then on the account's own space takes only sessions that have shown the
password (`password_sign_in_required`, see "The user's own space"): this session,
which was made through a provider and set the password without being asked for
one, opens it no more until it gives the password (`confirmPassword`). Its
websocket connections stay open and hear no more of the space; those of the
account's other sessions are closed.

Once only: an account that has a password is 409, and changes it with
`changePassword`. The password must have at least 8 characters and at most 1024
bytes; otherwise the request is 400 and `errors` names `password`.

post.description:
Takes the session as one that has shown the account's password: for a session made
through an organization's provider, to which the account's own space is closed once
the account has a password (`password_sign_in_required`, see "The user's own
space"). From then until the session ends it opens the space as a session made
with the password does, `getMyWorkspaces` lists the space with `passwordRequired`
false, and it goes on opening what it opened of the organizations: nothing else
changes of what it opens, and an organization that takes only sessions made
through another provider stays closed to it (`sso_required`). A session made with
the password is answered the same and opens what it opened.

The session goes on under a new cookie, as after `changePassword`: it opens more
than it did, and the value that opened less is no longer accepted. Its websocket
connections stay open, and are the confirmed session's from then on: what the
space refused them is asked again on the same connection.

A wrong password is 400 (not 401: the session is good) with the reason
`invalid_credentials`, and `errors` names `password`. Wrong ones are counted with
the failed logins to the account by its name, and too many are 429, also for a
login: the limits are those of `login`. An account that has no password
(`hasPassword` of `getMe`) is 409: its space takes any session, and there is
nothing to confirm. A password that was changed while this request was under way
is 409 too.

get.description:
Returns one page of the user's own time entries across every organization open to this
session, newest first (`startedAt DESC, id DESC`), together with `summary` totals over
every matching entry across all pages. Completed entries contribute `endedAt - startedAt`
to `summary`; a running entry (`endedAt` is `null`) is counted in `summary.count` and

post.description:
Makes the boards and wikis of an archive in the workspace, with the user as their
admin. The members the archive names for a board become members of it with the roles
they had, where they are in the workspace. The archive is sent before in parts: open an
upload with `createImportUpload`, send its parts with `putUploadPart`, then name
the upload here, in place of `completeUpload`. A part missing is 400 and the upload
stays open for it; otherwise the upload ends with the import, whether it succeeds or
not. Another user's upload, one that has ended, and one for another workspace are
404; an upload of a file is 400. A workspace the user is not in is 404 before the
body is read. For users of the workspace who are not guests, at the import as when
the upload was opened: a user who may not import any more is refused, and the upload
is thrown away.

The archive is of version 3, as the export routes write it. The formats of the
original (the line-based version 1 and the ZIP of version 2) and a ZIP without
`version.json` are 400, and nothing of them is stored. An archive of more than
10,000 entries, whose entries unpack to more than 1 GiB together, or with a
`board.jsonl` of more than 64 MiB (or a single JSONL line over 6 MiB) or a file larger
than `maxFileBytes` is 413 with the `limit` passed, and nothing of it is stored; for the
entry or line that is too large the reason is `archive_entry_too_large`. The blocks that show files are
pointed at the board's new copies of them, the images and file blocks of bodies
included. A file the board's line lists under `missingFiles` is not stored, even when
the archive has an entry of its name, and what shows it ends up showing no file. A card value that does not fit its property's kind is cleared, as a copy
does. A wiki of the archive (`kind` `wiki`) is made as a wiki, its pages and the
comments on them with it. What a write would refuse of an archive's boards, wikis
and blocks is 400 before any of them is stored, with the message the write has: a
block of a type of the other kind (a page on a board, a card on a wiki), a page
below anything but a page of its wiki or below a page the archive does not have,
pages that are each other's parents, a comment on anything but a card or page, a
wiki that is a template, and a wiki deeper or with more pages than the
organization's limits allow (400 with the reason `page_too_deep` or
`too_many_pages`).

The boards are made one after the other, not all or none: when one of them fails,
those before it stay. The members of a board who are not in the workspace are left
out of it, a guest of the workspace keeps no role above editor; the answer says how
many users were left out, not who.

A user runs one import at a time, and the server as many as its setting
`max_concurrent_imports` (2 unless set). Over either it is 429 with the reason
`import_running` or `server_imports_busy`; the upload stays open, to be named again.

Optional `format` selects `"fvoci"` (default, `.boardarchive`/`.zip`), `"trello"`
(`.json`), or `"notion"` (`.zip`). External formats commit all boards, wikis, blocks,
and bundled local files atomically: any validation, limit, or storage failure leaves
nothing stored. Returns a structured `ImportSummary` with counts, newly created
container identifiers, native `membersLeftOut`, and bounded `skipped` / `warnings`.

get.description:
An archive of the board with its blocks, its files and its members, offered as a
download with its length. For the board's members. The archive is a ZIP of version
3: `version.json`, and per board a directory with `board.jsonl` (one `board`,
`block` or `boardMember` per line, in the shapes of this contract, bodies included,
but that a block and a member name their board or wiki `boardId`, not `containerId`)
and the files the blocks show, those of the images and file blocks of bodies among
them. A board's line also carries `fileNames`: the name of each of its files, by
stored name, which an import gives the files it stores. A name an upload could not
have (blank, `.` or `..` after its last `/` or `\`, with U+0000, over 255 characters, or of another extension than the
stored name) is passed over and its file keeps the name of its entry, and an archive
without the member is read as before. A file a block shows that the board does not
have, its record or its bytes gone, gets no entry: it is listed under `missingFiles`
of the board's line, by stored name. A wiki is written as a board is, its `kind` `wiki`: its
pages as they stand and the comments on them are its blocks (not the pages in its
trash, nor the versions of bodies).

A user runs one export at a time, and the server as many as its setting
`max_concurrent_exports` (2 unless set). Over either it is 429 with the reason
`export_running` or `server_exports_busy`, and is to be asked for again later. An
export runs until its archive is sent or the client goes away; a download that takes
nothing for `export_stall_seconds` (60 unless set) is given up, and its connection
broken before the archive's end.

post.description:
Copies a board with its blocks, except comments, as a board or as a template. The
user becomes the admin of the copy, which is always private. A copy of the same kind
has the title of the original with ` copy` after it; a template made from a board is
titled `New board template`, and a board made from a template keeps the title. The
server writes those words in English and in Korean (` 사본`, `새 보드 템플릿`), and
chooses by the language of the user's settings; where the settings leave the language
to the device, or name one the server does not write in, by the first of the two that
`Accept-Language` prefers; failing both, English. The board's members may copy it; an
open template is for everyone in its workspace, and a built-in template for everyone.

A wiki is copied as a board is, with its pages as they stand: their tree and order,
titles, icons and bodies, the images and file blocks of the bodies given files of
their own, and what a body names among the wiki's pages named in the copy by its
copy (what it names elsewhere stays as it was). The comments on the pages, the
versions of their bodies, the pages in the trash, the wiki's other members and teams
and its public link are not copied. A wiki is no template: `asTemplate=true` is 400.
A copy deeper or with more pages than the organization's limits allow, lowered since
the wiki grew, is 400 with the reason `page_too_deep` or `too_many_pages` and the
`limit`.

Every file is sent as `application/octet-stream` and offered as a download
(`Content-Disposition: attachment`) under the name it was uploaded with, which
`getFileInfo` has: `filename*` carries that name, and `filename` the `fileId` for a

download: the `Last-Modified` of an answer is the time of that answer, so a request
with the `If-Modified-Since` of an earlier answer gets the whole file again.

parts are and how many; send each with `putUploadPart`, in any order and again
after a failure, then `completeUpload`. A file larger than `maxFileBytes` of
`getClientConfig` is 413 with the reason `file_too_large`. A user has at most 8

open uploads hold back at most what it is configured for: an upload over one of
these is 429, with the reason `too_many_uploads`, `uploads_pending` or
`server_uploads_pending`. An upload is open until it is completed, abandoned or
ends; one that ends is thrown away with its parts within the hour. For editors, as
`uploadFile`.

get.summary: The outline of a course

post.description:
The server chooses the identifier, the creator, the times and the `order`. For
editors of the course. With `kind` `unit` (also when left out), the unit goes below
`parentId`, a chapter of the same course (400 at `/parentId` otherwise), or at the
top of the course. With `kind` `chapter`, the chapter is a title-only heading at the
top of the course (`parentId` must be empty; 400 at `/parentId` otherwise) with no
body and no room. Among the siblings of that parent it goes right after `after` (400
at `/after` if that is no sibling of the same parent), first if `after` is empty, and
last if it is left out. A unit's body is written by `patchUnit`, or together in its
room (`JOIN_DOC`).

A course holds at most 2,000 units and 200 chapters, those in the trash not counted
(chapters do not count toward the 2,000-unit limit): one more unit is 400 with the
reason `too_many_units` and the `limit`, and one more chapter is 400 with the reason
`too_many_chapters` and the `limit`.

The course's listeners are told with `UPDATE_BLOCK`, whose block of the `type` `unit`
or `chapter` carries its `order` among its `fields`. Any sibling numbered anew to
leave room is told of too.

Enrolled members of any role (viewer, commenter, editor, admin, including invited
guests) and personal-space owners may record their own progress; an unjoined reader
of an open course is refused with 403 until they join the course.

timestamp. Setting `completed: false` clears `completedAt` to `null`. Omitting
`completed` or `lastPosition` preserves the existing value; sending `lastPosition:
null` clears it. Personal progress writes never broadcast over websockets, never
enter search indexes or archives, and emit no webhooks or audit logs. Chapters,
trashed units, units of another course, and non-course containers answer 404.

post.description:
A diary has one entry a day. The entry of `date` is made (201) with its mood, weather
and place; where the day has an entry, that entry is answered as it is (200) and
nothing of the request is stored, so of two requests that make the entry of one day
at once, one makes it and the other is answered with it. The server chooses the
identifier, the creator and the times. The body of the entry is written by
`patchDiaryEntry`, or together in its room (`JOIN_DOC`).

`date` is the day as the writer's own calendar has it, which the server does not
know: it must be a day of the calendar (`2026-02-30` is 400 at `/date`), and no more
than two days after the server's own day in UTC (400 at `/date`), which every time
zone's today is within. A day in the past is written as any other. The day of an
entry never changes afterwards.

A diary has at most 40,000 entries, those in the trash not counted: one more is 400
with the reason `too_many_entries` and the `limit`. An entry in the trash holds no
day: its day takes a new entry.

The user's other sessions are told with `UPDATE_BLOCK`, whose block of the `type`
`entry` has the day as its `title` and the day, mood, weather and place among its
`fields`.

get.summary: The invitations of a workspace

post.description:
Makes a link that lets whoever accepts it into the workspace, and answers it with
its `token`: the one time the token is told, as the server keeps its digest only. A
link ends seven days after it was made, or when it is revoked, and lets nobody in
from the moment who made it could no longer make it.

With the `role` `member` the link makes members of the workspace, as often as it is
used, and names no board. Only the workspace's administrators make one: anybody
else who works there is refused (403). Whoever accepts it becomes a member of the
workspace's organization too.

With the `role` `guest` the link lets one person, once, onto the board or the wiki
`containerId` of the workspace, in the role `containerRole` (`viewer`, `commenter` or
`editor`; an editor if left out): a guest of the workspace, who sees that board or
wiki and nothing else of it.
Who adds members to the board makes one (its admins, and the workspace's
administrators), while the workspace lets guests be invited
(`setGuestInvitations`); anybody else who sees the board is refused (403), and a
board the user does not see, or of another workspace, is not there (404). A
template takes no guests (400).

A guest of the workspace is told that it is not there (404).

post.description:
Queues a separate message for each unique email address with an existing link.
The token must name an invitation of this workspace that is neither revoked nor
ended (a member link must let somebody in still), and the sender must still be
allowed to make that kind of invitation. The same checks are repeated before each
delivery. A member link is sent as it is, its expiry and uses unchanged.
A guest link lets one person in once, so it is not sent: each recipient gets a
one-use guest link of their own, to the same board or wiki in the same role and ending
with it, made by the sender as their message leaves, naming the named link as its
`parentId` and the address as its `recipient` (and revoked if that message is
refused for good or given up). The named link is left as it is; messages go out
whether or not it was used, and revoking it revokes its children nobody used.
Invalid recipients reject the whole request before sending.
Each message is in the recipient's language when the mail is written in it, else the
sender's setting, else `language`, else English. A server that sends no mail answers 404.
A request names at most `invitation_mail_recipients` addresses, repeats counted
(400, `too_many_recipients`). Its messages are queued all or none: 429
(`invitation_mail_limit`, with `Retry-After`) when the workspace would pass
`invitation_mail_per_hour` messages within an hour or its organization its own
hourly limit (`invitation_mail_per_org_hour`), and 503 (`mail_queue_full`) when the
server's invitation queue cannot hold them all, or, on a server of several
organizations, the organization's share of it (half of what the others leave, at
least one request). A refused request sends nothing.

get.description:
The cards of the boards, the pages of the wikis and the units of the courses of the
workspace that the user has a role on, their own or a team's, the pages of its open
wikis and the units of its open courses for who works there (an open board they have
not joined is not searched), and, in the workspace of the user's own space, the
entries of its diaries, whose title and body together hold every word of `q`. The
title of an entry is its day (`2026-11-21`). Chapters, comments, property values and
attached files are not searched, and neither are templates. How words match depends
on the server: with a search server, Korean is matched by its words, whatever
particles and endings they carry, and a compound by its parts too ("환불 규정" finds
"환불규정을"); without one, each word (what is between white space) is in the title
or the body as it is written there, ASCII letters in either case ("환불" finds
"환불규정을", "배포하다" does not find "배포합니다"). Each hit is the card, the page,
the entry or the unit as it is now: its `kind`, its `title`, the container it is in
(`containerId`, and `containerKind`, by which a client tells their addresses apart),
and `snippet`, a piece of its body in stretches of plain text, those that matched
marked; the snippet is empty for a body that changed a moment ago, or has nothing to
show. The best match first (without a search server: those whose title holds every
word, then the most recently changed). Nothing says how many match in all: fewer than
`limit` means that no more of what the user reads matches (for a user with a role on
more containers than a search names, 1,000 with a search server and 10,000 without:
among the 10,000 best matches of the workspace).

A `q` of more than 200 characters, a `kind` that is none and a `limit` outside 1
to 50 are 400; a `q` that is empty finds nothing. A user who searches more often
than the server lets one is told to wait (429, `Retry-After`). While the search
server does not answer, where it cannot hold its index, or where a search takes more
than three seconds, the answer is 503 with the reason `search_unavailable`: nothing
else of the server waits for it, and the database does not stand in for a search
server.

room left between them (two of one order, or orders grown long), they are numbered

post.description:
Copies the page with every page below it, within its wiki, for editors of the wiki:
the copy goes right after the page among its siblings, titled `title` if given (the
page's own title otherwise; a client names it in its reader's language), and the
pages below it are copied below it as they are, with their titles, icons, places and
bodies, what is typed in them now included. The images and file blocks in the bodies
get files of their own, as a card's duplicate's do. The versions of the bodies and
the comments are not copied. The tree is held to the organization's limits: 400 with
the reason `page_too_deep` or `too_many_pages` (with the `limit`) if the copies
would be deeper, or the wiki larger, than they let it be; 400 at `/title` for a
title longer than 16383 characters. Nothing is changed then.

The wiki's members are told with `UPDATE_BLOCK` of each copy, a page before those
below it, and of each page of the parent numbered anew to leave the copy room.

tags.description: Diaries and their entries, in the workspace of a user's own space and nowhere else. A diary is a board of the kind `diary` that holds one entry a day and nothing else; its owner alone reads it. What it shares with a board is asked under `/containers/{containerId}` with the diary's identifier: the diary itself (`getContainer`), its title, description and icon (`patchContainer`), the trash (`deleteContainer`, `undeleteContainer`, `getDeletedContainers`), its files and their versions and leases, its place in the sidebar, and its archive (`exportContainer`; the archive of the workspace holds its diaries, and an archive that is imported makes each diary anew, in the user's own space only). Its entries are found by `searchWorkspaceContent`, by their writer. What is about the people of a board answers 404 for a diary, as for an identifier of nothing: its members, joining and leaving it, its teams, its link (`/sharing`, `/shared/{containerId}`), invitations to it, and `duplicateContainer`. So do the operations under `/boards/{boardId}` and `/wikis/{wikiId}`: a diary has no blocks but its entries, no cards, no views, no pages, no comments and no templates; and no reference names an entry.
